The Hamiltonian is \( H = \varepsilon \vec{\sigma} \cdot \vec{n} \), where \(\vec{n}\) is a unit vector. The Pauli matrices satisfy \((\vec{\sigma} \cdot \vec{n})^2 = I\) for any unit vector \(\vec{n}\), so the eigenvalues of \(\vec{\sigma} \cdot \vec{n}\) are \(\pm 1\). Multiplying by the constant \(\varepsilon\) (which has dimensions of energy) gives the eigenvalues of \(H\) as \(+\varepsilon\) and \(-\varepsilon\).

Answer: D
